resolution_note_sup002_sup003: The earlier EALLOWREMOTE failure (iteration 3) was retried and traced to root cause rather than accepted: npm's dependency resolution was scanning bun's own nested node_modules/.bun/<pkg>/node_modules/... cache structure already present in the working tree, and trying to fetch a transitive devDependency's own devDependency (nyc, several levels deep inside an unrelated package's own test tooling) — not anything in this repo's actual dependency tree. Confirmed by running the identical `npm install --package-lock-only` in a directory containing only package.json with no bun-managed node_modules present: it succeeded cleanly (211 packages resolved, real package-lock.json generated). That lockfile was regenerated against the full monorepo (a clean `git clone` with the exact-pin edit applied, packages/* present, no node_modules) and used for a real end-to-end verification: `npm ci --ignore-scripts` (exit 0), `npm run build` (exit 0), `npm run test` (73 files / 547 tests, exit 0), `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high` (0 vulnerabilities). The real fix — pinning the three root @alexvegman/* devDependencies to their exact published versions (0.1.0) instead of workspace:*, plus the committed package-lock.json — was then applied to the actual repo, re-verified there with `bun install` (no changes — bun still resolves to the local workspace packages, confirming the exact-version pin doesn't break day-to-day bun-based development) and a full `bun run build && bun run lint && bun run test` pass. A dedicated `npm-compat` job was added to .github/workflows/ci.yml running the same four commands on every push/PR, so this stays a real, continuously-enforced check rather than a one-time local verification.
